subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explain: One byte is made up of exactly 8 bits.

questions.q: A washing machine contains a microcontroller dedicated to running its wash cycles. This is an example of:
questions.explain: A dedicated computer built into a larger device to perform a fixed task is an embedded system.

questions.q: What is virtual memory?
options: A section of secondary storage used as if it were RAM when RAM is full
A type of ROM that stores the operating system
Extra cache built into the CPU
Cloud storage accessed over the internet
questions.explain: Virtual memory uses part of the hard disk/SSD as additional RAM when the physical RAM becomes full.

questions.q: Which storage medium is read using a laser?
options: Optical disc such as a DVD
questions.explain: Optical media such as CDs and DVDs are read by a laser detecting pits and lands on the disc surface.

questions.q: Which type of primary memory is volatile, meaning its contents are lost when power is removed?
questions.explain: RAM is volatile, so all its contents are lost when the computer is switched off.

questions.q: What is the role of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) in the CPU?
options: It carries out arithmetic calculations and logical operations
It connects the CPU to secondary storage
It decodes instructions and manages the fetch-execute cycle
It permanently stores the operating system
questions.explain: The ALU performs all arithmetic (such as addition) and logical (such as comparisons) operations.

questions.q: Which storage type would be most suitable for distributing a film to be sold in shops and read in a player?
options: Optical disc such as a Blu-ray
questions.explain: Optical discs are cheap to mass-produce and are read by a laser, making them suitable for distributing films.

questions.q: Which list places units of storage in order from smallest to largest?
questions.explain: A bit is the smallest unit, then a byte, then a kilobyte, then a megabyte.

questions.q: Which register holds the address of the memory location that is about to be read from or written to?
questions.explain: The MAR holds the address of the memory location the CPU is about to access.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a role of the operating system?
options: Managing files and the file system
questions.explain: Editing a document is done by application software; the operating system manages hardware, memory, files and processes.

questions.q: Why can a dual-core CPU often process tasks faster than a single-core CPU at the same clock speed?
options: It has a faster clock speed automatically
Cores remove the need for any cache
It can execute multiple instructions simultaneously across its cores
Each core stores the operating system separately
questions.explain: Multiple cores allow several instructions to be processed at the same time (in parallel).

questions.q: What is an embedded system?
options: A general-purpose computer that runs many different applications
A computer built into a larger device to perform a dedicated task
A network of computers sharing files over the internet
Software that translates high-level code into machine code
questions.explain: An embedded system is a computer dedicated to a specific function within a larger device, such as a washing machine controller.

questions.q: Which register stores the instruction that has just been fetched, ready to be decoded?
questions.explain: The Current Instruction Register holds the instruction currently being decoded and executed.

questions.q: Which is an example of utility software?
questions.explain: Defragmentation software is utility software that maintains and optimises the computer system.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of cache memory in a CPU?
options: To replace the need for RAM entirely
To hold frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU for fast access
To store data permanently when the computer is switched off
To increase the total amount of secondary storage
questions.explain: Cache is small, very fast memory that stores frequently accessed data so the CPU does not have to wait for slower RAM.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of system software?
questions.explain: The operating system is system software that manages the computer's hardware and resources, unlike application software.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Accumulator (ACC) in the CPU?
options: To store the operating system permanently
To temporarily store the results of calculations from the ALU
To store the address of the next instruction
To hold the address of the memory being accessed
questions.explain: The Accumulator temporarily holds the intermediate results of arithmetic and logic operations.

questions.q: Which secondary storage type uses spinning platters and read/write heads to store data magnetically?
questions.explain: A magnetic hard disk drive stores data on spinning platters that are magnetised by read/write heads.

questions.q: During the fetch stage, which register holds the address of the NEXT instruction to be fetched?
questions.explain: The Program Counter stores the address of the next instruction to be fetched and is incremented each cycle.

questions.q: A larger CPU cache generally improves performance because it:
options: Increases the amount of secondary storage
Reduces how often the CPU must wait for data from slower RAM
questions.explain: A bigger cache lets more frequently used data sit close to the CPU, reducing waits for slower RAM.

questions.q: Which statement about ROM is correct?
options: It is volatile and loses its contents when switched off
It is non-volatile and typically holds the boot/start-up instructions
It is used as the computer's main working memory
It can be easily rewritten thousands of times during normal use
questions.explain: ROM is non-volatile and usually stores the start-up (boot) instructions the computer needs when first switched on.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the von Neumann architecture?
options: The CPU has no need for any registers
Program instructions and data are stored in the same memory
Programs are stored permanently in the ALU
Instructions and data are stored in physically separate memories
questions.explain: In the von Neumann architecture a single shared memory holds both program instructions and the data they operate on.
